results.title: The Many Uses of the Parthenon

evidence.summaryExcerpt: The name comes from the Greek parthénos, meaning "maiden" or "virgin". The most common explanation ties it to Athena's cult title. Other explanations exist: Maidens' sacrifice: One suggestion is that the name alludes to the maidens (parthénoi) whose sacrifice was believed to protect the city. A room, not the whole temple: The name may originally have applied to a single room. Overall, the consensus is that the name derives from parthénos and Athena's virgin epithet, though scholars disagree on whether the name was official or originally applied to a room.

claimResults.note: Every source agrees the name comes from Greek parthenos, 'maiden' or 'virgin', and the summary calls the link to Athena Parthenos the most common explanation, but it also reports scholarly alternatives: the maidens, a single room of the temple, a later nickname. An etymology stated as settled, so it cannot be confirmed as written.

evidence.restatement: Phidias's colossal gold-and-ivory statue, the Athena Parthenos, stood inside the temple.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: The name's origin is still debated. The main competing explanations are these: ... The traditional view is that "Parthenon" means roughly "temple of the virgin goddess," tied to the cult of Athena Parthenos. ... Scholars have argued that the term seems to have originally referred only to a particular room of the Parthenon; it is debated which room this is, and how the room acquired its name.

claimResults.note: Not confirmed as written. The Athena Parthenos derivation is the traditional view, but the name may first have meant a room (the maidens' chamber), and a further theory ties it to the Erechtheion's caryatids. All views agree only that parthenos means maiden or virgin.

evidence.restatement: Phidias made the colossal gold-and-ivory statue of Athena that stood inside the Parthenon.
